solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird seeing rat around entrance to hole

indicators.note: around means the informing word wraps the letter from the hole

parts.note: to rat is to inform on someone; in British slang to cough is likewise to confess or grass

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter, so this picks the start of hole

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a rat nosing about the mouth of a burrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like the animal from the surface, but it is a verb: to inform, which British slang also calls to cough.
explanation.definitionFit: The chough is a red-billed member of the crow family found on coastal cliffs.

clue.text: Type of leg spinning ace maintaining zip and length

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the shuffled ace holds the zip and length letters
spinning sends the letters of ace whirling into a new order

parts.note: zip means energy or verve, which is brio

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator describes a leg-spinning ace bowling with zip and good length.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket (leg spin, length), but the leg is a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriole is a curved furniture leg, bulging outwards at the knee and tapering to an ornamental foot, typical of Queen Anne chairs.

clue.text: Players from promoted Barrow lacking wingers around box

indicators.note: around means the turned letters are split to enclose the box word
in a down answer, promoted means moved upwards, so the letters are read bottom to top
the wingers of a word are its outside letters, so Barrow loses its first and last

parts.note: a chest is a box or trunk

explanation.surface: Barrow, the football club just promoted, has no wingers and plays a defensive game around the penalty box.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrow is a Cumbrian football club, so 'promoted' and 'wingers' sound like football, but they are reversal and trimming signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a body of musicians, the players who perform together.

clue.text: Good mimic's facial expression

parts.note: to ape is to mimic; the 's stands for is, joining the wordplay to the definition

explanation.surface: An impressionist's skill shows in their face.
explanation.definitionFit: A gape is a wide-open stare of astonishment, a look worn on the face.

clue.text: Ruin jewellery that's seen in joint?

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
bling is flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a piece of jewellery by spotting it inside a hinge or joint.
explanation.walkthrough: The joint is not a hinge but a joint of meat; the question mark flags that the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbling is the streaky pattern of fat running through a good cut of beef or other meat.

clue.text: Article supports test probing boxer dog

indicators.note: in a down answer, a word that supports another sits beneath it, so the article goes at the bottom
probing means poking inside, so the test goes into the boxer

parts.note: Muhammad Ali is the crossword's favourite boxer
SAT is a standard school test
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammar point props up a test that pokes at a boxer dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer dog' reads as one breed, but the boxer is Ali and dog alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alsatian is the British name for the German Shepherd breed of dog.

clue.text: Spike, every time, sent up 1960s film

parts.note: a barb is a sharp point or spike

indicators.note: in a down answer, sent up means read from bottom to top, so the letters of every time are turned

parts.note: every here means all
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Spike Milligan or a critic sends up an old sixties movie every time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' suggests parody, but it only reverses ALL ERA to ARELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarella is the 1968 science-fiction film starring Jane Fonda as the space adventurer.

clue.text: Method of drinking at home over lunchtime?

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: in means at home
one o'clock is a typical lunchtime

explanation.surface: Someone drinks at home over a long lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: To drink something 'down in one' is to swallow it in a single go.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes downing a drink at a single swallow, a style of drinking.

clue.text: Greedy type with good news: meal turning up outside

indicators.note: outside means the turned meal wraps around the news letters
in a down answer, turning up means reading the meal word bottom to top

parts.note: tea is a light evening meal in Britain
news is read as the plural of new, so two Ns

explanation.surface: A glutton hears good news: a meal is arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'News' is treated as the plural of 'new', one N for each.
explanation.definitionFit: Gannet is British slang for a greedy eater, from the seabird's reputation for gulping fish.

clue.text: Perhaps infant class in Edale's outskirts finding avian habitat

indicators.note: in means the class goes inside the outer letters
the outskirts of Edale are its first and last letters

parts.note: Year 1, written YR I, is a class in an English infant school; perhaps marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A school class visiting the edge of Edale finds a bird's nest.
explanation.walkthrough: Edale is a village in the Peak District. Year 1 is the second year of English primary school, part of the infant stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the nest of an eagle or other bird of prey, high on a crag.

clue.text: Overdue funds to support annual party not right

parts.note: to back is to support

indicators.note: not means the right letters are taken away from party

parts.note: taken as the word itself before letters are removed

explanation.surface: Money owed is put towards the yearly do, which went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTY without RT leaves PAY. 'annual' has no job in the wordplay; the blog and its commenters agree it seems left over from an earlier version of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Back pay is wages owed for work done earlier, money that is late in reaching the worker.

clue.text: Master with circus animal, essentially switching piece of meat

parts.note: sir is a title of respect for a master

indicators.note: essentially points at the core of the word, and switching swaps those two middle letters

parts.note: a lion is a classic circus animal

explanation.surface: A ringmaster and his lion swap places at the heart of the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirloin is a prime cut of beef from the upper loin.

clue.text: Fickle lad oddly ignored retailer

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters keeps the second, fourth, sixth and eighth of the two words

explanation.surface: A capricious young man snubs a shopkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: IKEA is the Swedish flat-pack furniture chain, a household-goods store.

clue.text: Asian celebrity interrupts Stevie performing

indicators.note: interrupts means breaking into the middle of the shuffled letters
performing suggests Stevie's letters are put through their paces into a new order

parts.note: a name is a famous person, as in a big name

explanation.surface: A star cuts into Stevie Wonder's stage set.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vietnamese person comes from Vietnam in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: A Gallic rocker Vincent awfully sour and mean

parts.note: un is French for a
Gene Vincent was the American rock and roll singer of Be-Bop-A-Lula

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of sour are in a terrible mess

explanation.surface: A French rock fan finds Gene Vincent bitter and stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Gallic' means the French word for a.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungenerous and mean both describe someone stingy, unwilling to give or share.

clue.text: List books, it doesn't matter which

parts.note: lit, short for literature, means books collectively
any means whichever one, it doesn't matter which

explanation.surface: Someone asked to list some books replies that any will do.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a long recital or catalogue, as in a litany of complaints.

clue.text: Athletics event broadcast live during start of year

indicators.note: during means the shuffled letters sit inside the month

parts.note: January, JAN, is the start of the year

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of live are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A field event is shown live on television in early January.
explanation.definitionFit: The javelin throw is an Olympic field event where a spear is hurled for distance.

clue.text: Struggle in winter relocating conference

indicators.note: in means the struggle word goes inside the reordered letters
relocating moves the letters of winter about into a new order

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: A battle to move a conference to a new venue in the winter.
explanation.definitionFit: An interview is a formal meeting or consultation, often between a journalist and a subject.

clue.text: Slough's yearly meeting written in paper

definitions.note: the 's means is, so the definition is just slough, a bog

indicators.note: written in means the meeting letters are set inside the paper word

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
AGM is short for annual general meeting

explanation.surface: The town of Slough's annual meeting is reported in the local paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it is a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a muddy swamp, and a quagmire is soft boggy ground.

clue.text: Drum Terry emptied with cooking vessel in silence

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside letters, leaving only the first and last of Terry
in means the pan sits inside the silence word

parts.note: mum means silence, as in keep mum
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A drummer called Terry bangs a saucepan in a hush.
explanation.definitionFit: The tympanum is the eardrum, and also a term for a drum such as a kettledrum.

clue.text: Sweet things Georgia and mate, possibly united, kiss

parts.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia
maté is a South American herbal tea, so possibly a tea
U is an abbreviation for united, as in football team names
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A woman named Georgia and her partner, perhaps married, share a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like a partner; it is maté, the South American herbal drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Gâteaux are rich cream cakes, sweet desserts in French style.

clue.text: Loose liquid waste, tons taking over rivers

indicators.note: taking over means the tons letters replace the rivers letters

parts.note: slurry is liquid manure or waste
R is an abbreviation for river, so rivers gives two
T is an abbreviation for ton, so tons gives two

explanation.surface: Tons of liquid sewage overflow into the rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Slutty is a derogatory word for sexually promiscuous, a sense of loose.

clue.text: Award lifted after, say, strong punch?

indicators.note: after means the award comes after the say letters

parts.note: EG, for example, means say

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifted means raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gong is British slang for a medal or award

explanation.surface: A boxer gets an award after a mighty punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch is the drink, not a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a drink of eggs, milk and spirits, often a potent festive punch.

clue.text: Number of small flat

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
even means flat, level

explanation.surface: Someone counts up the rooms in a small apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven is a whole number, between six and eight.

clue.text: Chap with score below par succeeded here?

definitions.text: Chap with score below par succeeded here?

parts.note: Glen is a man's name
an eagle is a golf score of two under par
S is an abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A man scores an eagle and wins at a famous course.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a description: a golfer scoring an eagle triumphs at this course.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleneagles in Perthshire is a famous Scottish golf resort, which hosted the 2014 Ryder Cup.

clue.text: Musical European full of life mostly

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: vital means lively, full of life

explanation.surface: A lively European person, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice stage show about Eva Perón.

clue.text: On which one's wasted time with farewell message

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the farewell on a gravestone

explanation.surface: Someone has wasted time with a goodbye note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' is slang for very drunk or high: a drug trip is something one is wasted on.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a hallucinogenic drug experience, during which the user is intoxicated.

clue.text: Heard American apology maybe for attire

indicators.note: heard means the apology is said aloud, pronounced

parts.note: sorry, said in an American accent, sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: An American is heard apologising for their outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: In many American accents sorry is pronounced 'sahri'; 'maybe' allows that the accent varies.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is the draped garment worn by women in South Asia, a form of dress.

clue.text: Rain dancing which sorcerers perform somewhere in Africa

indicators.note: dancing jiggles the letters of rain into a new order

parts.note: obi, or obeah, is a form of sorcery practised in the Caribbean

explanation.surface: Witch doctors perform a rain dance somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya in East Africa.

clue.text: Leading story reflected joy

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: leading means number one, written NO I
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: The front-page story mirrored a nation's happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' is No. 1, with the one as a Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness and exhilaration, a synonym for joy.

clue.text: Informed about fine method of beef production?

indicators.note: about means the informing word goes around the fine letter

parts.note: grassed is British slang for informed on someone to the police
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Someone told on a farmer over a fine for their beef-rearing method.
explanation.walkthrough: To grass on someone is British slang for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass-fed cattle graze on pasture rather than grain, a way of raising beef.

clue.text: Old party band from 1980s, repeatedly trashing hotel lodge

indicators.note: trashing means destroying, and repeatedly means it happens to both words

parts.note: the Whigs were a historic British political party
Wham! was George Michael's 1980s pop duo
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet; repeatedly gives one for each word

explanation.surface: A former party band trashes a hotel room again and again, as rock stars do.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigwam is a domed Native American dwelling, a hut or lodge.
